summary: Follow Lia’s sneaker order as a one-server store adds capacity, queues and regional recovery.
scope: An illustrative store based on the scaling chapter of system-design-notes. Each scene highlights one architectural decision. The diagrams show example routes and contain no measured traffic or capacity claims.
author: Thoth

sources.title: PostgreSQL · Standby servers and streaming replication
Amazon CloudFront · How CloudFront delivers content

componentNotes.client: Lia uses the same product page and checkout across all nine steps. The store and its workload are illustrative.
componentNotes.lb: Routes API requests to healthy app servers in the active region. The DNS failover step covers switching regions.
componentNotes.sessions: Sign-in state lives in a shared store, so another app server can serve the next request.
componentNotes.replica: A lagging replica can show older data. Read the primary for a purchase just confirmed to the customer.
componentNotes.cache: The app caches product details on read. Cache expiration and invalidation determine how long a change can be missing from the cached view.
componentNotes.cdn: An edge hit returns the image near the viewer. On a miss the CDN fetches the object from the origin.
componentNotes.relay: Reads committed outbox rows and publishes receipt jobs. Storing the event with the order avoids losing it between the database commit and publishing.
componentNotes.worker: The worker uses the order ID to recognize retried jobs and acknowledges delivery after the receipt is sent.
componentNotes.router: This example routes by a hash of order ID at the application layer. Cross-shard reporting needs a separate query or aggregation strategy.
componentNotes.dns: This example uses active-passive DNS failover. DNS supplies an address. The phone then sends the HTTPS checkout to the chosen destination.
componentNotes.standby-db: A replicated copy must be safe to promote before the standby region accepts checkout writes. In an asynchronous design, recent commits can be missing from the recovered copy.
